intro: Thai food is getting friendlier and friendlier for plant eaters — there are vegetarian restaurants, jay (vegan) restaurants, and veggie dishes at ordinary places too. The key is to understand the difference between "jay" and "vegetarian" and to know the ordering phrases, because some veggie dishes still get fish sauce or shrimp paste added. This article rounds up the words you need to know, the easiest cities, and the vegetarian festival.
quickAnswerHtml: Eating vegan/vegetarian in Thailand has gotten much easier. "Jay" (เจ) means strict vegan (no meat, nothing from animals, no pungent vegetables — look for the yellow flag with the เจ character), while "mangsawirat" (มังสวิรัติ) means vegetarian (may include egg/dairy). Watch out for veggie dishes that still get fish sauce, shrimp paste, or oyster sauce added — order "Kin jay" or "Mai sai neua, mai sai nam pla" (no meat, no fish sauce). Chiang Mai and Bangkok are the easiest cities for finding restaurants.

blocks.html: Thai cooking is built on plenty of vegetables, tofu, and fruit, but "looks vegetarian" and "is actually vegetarian" aren't the same thing, because many dishes are seasoned with fish sauce, shrimp paste, oyster sauce, or bone broth. Understanding the vocabulary and ordering correctly is the trick that lets you eat with peace of mind.

blocks.text: Jay vs vegetarian — what's the difference

blocks.caption: Two words you need to tell apart
rows: Strict vegan — no meat, egg, or dairy, and no pungent vegetables (garlic, onion). Look for the yellow flag with the เจ character.
Mangsawirat (มังสวิรัติ)
Vegetarian — no meat, but may include egg or dairy.
Veggie dishes at ordinary restaurants; may still have fish sauce/shrimp paste added.

items: "Kin jay" (I eat vegan/jay) — signals strict vegan (understood easily nationwide)
"Mai sai neua sat" (no meat) — leave out the meat
"Mai sai nam pla" (no fish sauce) — very important; many dishes get fish sauce even when they look like vegetables
"Mai sai kapi / mai sai hoy nang rom" (no shrimp paste / no oyster sauce) — avoid animal-based seasonings
"Mangsawirat, tan khai dai/mai dai" (vegetarian, with/without egg) — state your level clearly

blocks.text: Dishes that are easy to make plant-based

blocks.html: Many dishes can be adapted to plant-based, such as stir-fried mixed vegetables, pad kaprao with tofu/mushroom, vegetable fried rice, jay pad thai, jay som tam (no fermented fish or dried shrimp), green curry with tofu, and fresh fruit. Most made-to-order shops can cook a veggie version if you say so clearly. Restaurants with an "aahaan jay" or "mangsawirat" sign are the most worry-free to order from.

blocks.text: Easiest cities for restaurants, and the vegetarian festival

items.title: Chiang Mai
items.text: The most vegan- and vegetarian-friendly city, with lots of cafés and vegan restaurants.

items.title: Bangkok
items.text: Plenty of vegan/vegetarian restaurants, especially around Sukhumvit and Ari, plus jay food stalls at the markets.

items.title: Vegetarian festival (Oct)
items.text: During the 9-day festival, especially in Phuket, the whole town fills up with jay food — a paradise for vegans.

items.title: Look for the yellow flag

faq.a: "Jay" (เจ) means strict vegan — no meat, egg, or dairy, and no pungent vegetables (garlic, onion). Look for the yellow flag with the เจ character. "Mangsawirat" (มังสวิรัติ) means vegetarian — no meat, but it may include egg or dairy.

faq.q: Is there hidden meat in Thai vegetable dishes?
faq.a: There can be. Many dishes that look like vegetables are still seasoned with fish sauce, shrimp paste, oyster sauce, or bone broth. Order "Kin jay" (I eat vegan) or "Mai sai neua, mai sai nam pla" (no meat, no fish sauce) to be clear.

faq.q: What are the most important ordering phrases?
faq.a: "Kin jay" (for vegan) and "Mai sai nam pla" (no fish sauce) are the two phrases that help the most, because fish sauce is an animal-based seasoning that ends up in many veggie dishes.

faq.q: Which city is easiest for finding vegan restaurants?
faq.a: Chiang Mai is the most vegan- and vegetarian-friendly city, followed by Bangkok (the Sukhumvit and Ari areas). And during the vegetarian festival in October, the whole town of Phuket fills up with jay food.

faq.q: What kind of restaurant is the most worry-free to order from?
faq.a: Restaurants flying a yellow flag or showing an "aahaan jay"/"mangsawirat" sign already cook without anything from animals, so you can order any dish without worrying about fish sauce or shrimp paste.
